text: Starting with what is your problem or what is your goal? I would say this is a bigger challenge than most people recognize or realize. 80% of the folks that I work with, this is their biggest problem.
speaker: Nicole Forsgren
context: Nicole is discussing one of the most fundamental challenges in developer productivity work. She emphasizes that the majority of teams she works with struggle with clearly defining their objectives before starting improvement initiatives. Teams often spend months working on vague directives like "improve developer experience" without having a clear understanding of what specific aspect they should focus on, leading to wasted effort and confusion.
text_ko: 먼저 문제나 목표가 무엇인지부터 명확히 해야 해요. 이건 대부분 사람들이 생각하는 것보다 훨씬 더 큰 도전이에요. 제가 함께 일하는 사람들 중 80%에게 이게 가장 큰 문제예요.
text_zh: 先问自己：你到底遇到什么问题，或者你想达到什么目标？我觉得这比大多数人想的要难多了。我合作的客户里，大概有80%的人把这当成他们最主要的问题。
text_es: Empieza por preguntarte: ¿cuál es tu problema o qué quieres lograr? Diría que es un reto mayor de lo que la mayoría cree. El 80% de la gente con la que trabajo tiene esto como su principal problema.
key_sentence: This is a bigger challenge than most people recognize or realize.
original_text: Starting with what is your problem or what is your goal? I would say this is a bigger challenge than most people recognize or realize. 80% of the folks that I work with, this is their biggest problem. Even at executive levels, teams will have gone off for several months, and they're tackling something, and they'll come back with uncertainty, and they'll say like, "Well, you told me to improve developer experience."

vocabulary.definition: A difficult task or situation that requires effort and determination to overcome.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business environment, a 'challenge' may refer to obstacles faced in achieving goals, such as market competition or resource limitations.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a sense of opportunity for growth and innovation, rather than just a negative hurdle.

vocabulary.definition: To identify or acknowledge something as valid or important.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of business, 'recognize' is often used when acknowledging achievements, trends, or challenges that require attention.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can carry a connotation of awareness and validation, suggesting a deeper understanding of a situation.

text: I'm like, "Okay, what do you mean by this? Are you talking about inner and outer loop? Are you talking about friction? Are you talking about culture? But if you're talking about culture, this is totally different than if you're talking about friction in toolchains.
speaker: Nicole Forsgren
context: Nicole continues explaining why clear problem definition is crucial. She illustrates how "developer experience" can mean vastly different things - from technical toolchain issues to cultural problems - and teams need to be specific about which aspect they're addressing. Without this clarity, different team members may work toward completely different goals, making their efforts ineffective.
text_ko: 저는 "그러니까 이게 무슨 뜻이에요? 내부 루프(inner loop)랑 외부 루프(outer loop)를 말하는 건가요? 마찰(friction)을 말하는 건가요? 문화(culture)를 말하는 건가요? 근데 문화 얘기라면 툴체인(toolchains)에서의 마찰을 말할 때랑 완전히 달라요."라고 해요.
text_zh: 我就会说：“好吧，你到底什么意思？你是说内外循环(inner and outer loop)？还是在说摩擦(friction)？还是在说文化(culture)？但如果你说的是文化(culture)，那和你说的是工具链(toolchains)里的摩擦(friction)完全不是一回事。”
text_es: Yo digo: "Bueno, ¿a qué te refieres con esto? ¿Te refieres al bucle interno y externo (inner and outer loop)? ¿A fricción (friction)? ¿A cultura? Pero si hablas de cultura, eso es completamente distinto a si estás hablando de fricción en las cadenas de herramientas (toolchains)."
key_sentence: But if you're talking about culture, this is totally different than if you're talking about friction in toolchains.
original_text: I'm like, "Okay, what do you mean by this? Are you talking about inner and outer loop? Are you talking about friction? Are you talking about culture? But if you're talking about culture, this is totally different than if you're talking about friction in toolchains. If you're on different pages, you're heading in completely different directions."

vocabulary.definition: Friction refers to the resistance or obstacles that hinder progress or smooth operation within a process or system.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, friction often describes inefficiencies in workflows, toolchains, or user experiences that can impede productivity and innovation.
vocabulary.nuance: While friction can imply a negative aspect, it may also highlight areas for improvement and optimization within a system.

vocabulary.definition: Culture encompasses the shared values, beliefs, and practices that shape the behavior and interactions of individuals within an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, culture influences employee engagement, collaboration, and overall organizational effectiveness, often impacting recruitment and retention.
vocabulary.nuance: Culture can be both a strength and a challenge; it is essential to understand its nuances to foster a positive work environment.

text: So I started as a software engineer at IBM. I was writing software for large enterprise systems, which meant I ended up running them. So I was also a CIS admin. I was racking the stacking.
speaker: Nicole Forsgren
context: Nicole describes her early career background when Lenny asks about her unique journey. She explains how she started as a software engineer at IBM working on enterprise systems, which naturally led her to also become a system administrator managing large computing environments. The "seven-day march" refers to the grueling, unsustainable work pace that was common in traditional enterprise IT operations.
text_ko: 저는 IBM에서 소프트웨어 엔지니어(software engineer)로 시작했어요. 대규모 엔터프라이즈 시스템(enterprise systems)용 소프트웨어를 개발했는데, 그러다 보니 결국 그 시스템들을 직접 운영하게 됐어요. 그래서 CIS 관리자(CIS admin)도 맡았고, 장비를 랙에 올리고 배선하는(racking the stacking) 일까지 했어요.
text_zh: 我一开始在 IBM 当软件工程师 (software engineer)，给大型企业系统写软件。写完以后还得负责运行和维护这些系统，所以我也当起了 CIS 管理员 (CIS admin)，连把服务器上机架、拉线这些活儿都干过 (racking the stacking)。
text_es: Empecé como ingeniero de software en IBM. Desarrollaba software para grandes sistemas empresariales, así que al final también terminaba encargándome de operarlos. También hacía de administrador de sistemas (CIS admin) y me tocaba montar los racks y apilar los servidores (racking and stacking).
key_sentence: I was writing software for large enterprise systems, which meant I ended up running them.
original_text: So I started as a software engineer at IBM. I was writing software for large enterprise systems, which meant I ended up running them. So I was also a CIS admin. I was racking the stacking. I was running these really, really large labs, and then I kind of stumbled into this seven-day march for several years, and I was like, "There has to be a better way."

vocabulary.definition: Enterprise systems are large-scale software solutions designed to support and integrate the core business processes of an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, enterprise systems are crucial for managing operations, data, and resources across various departments, ensuring efficiency and consistency.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a level of complexity and scale that is not present in smaller software solutions, making it more suitable for large organizations.

vocabulary.definition: Admin, short for administrator, refers to a person responsible for managing and maintaining computer systems, networks, or software applications.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech environments, admins play a vital role in ensuring system security, user access, and overall operational efficiency.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'admin' can refer to various levels of administrative roles, it often connotes a technical focus, particularly in IT and software contexts.

vocabulary.definition: A software engineer is a professional who applies engineering principles to the design, development, testing, and maintenance of software applications.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, software engineers are essential for creating innovative solutions, improving existing systems, and ensuring that software meets user needs and business objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: The term emphasizes a technical and systematic approach to software development, distinguishing it from roles that may focus more on design or project management.

vocabulary.definition: Stacking refers to the arrangement or layering of software components or hardware systems to create a functional architecture.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, stacking is often discussed in relation to software stacks, which are combinations of technologies used to build applications and services.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a strategic choice of technologies that work well together, and is often used in discussions about system architecture and development practices.

text: And the joke there when we met with Gartner, they were like, "Your superpower here was that you tricked people into strategy," which was not only how do I benchmark? That was kind of our top-of-the-funnel. Everyone wants to know how they compare.
speaker: Nicole Forsgren
context: Nicole is describing feedback she received about DORA's business approach from Gartner analysts. She explains how DORA attracted customers initially through benchmarking services - allowing companies to compare their performance against industry standards - but the real value was in providing strategic guidance on improvement priorities. This created a pathway from measurement to actionable strategy.
text_ko: 가트너(Gartner)랑 만났을 때 웃긴 얘기가 있었는데, 가트너 쪽에서 "여러분의 슈퍼파워(superpower)는 사람들을 살짝 꾀어서 전략을 세우게 만든 거였어요"라고 하더라고요. 그건 단순히 "어떻게 벤치마크하죠?(benchmark)?"하는 문제만이 아니라, 사실 그게 우리 퍼널 상단(top-of-the-funnel)이었어요. 누구나 자기가 다른 사람들하고 어떻게 비교되는지 알고 싶어하니까요.
text_zh: 我们跟Gartner见面的时候，他们半开玩笑说：“你们的超能力就是把人骗着去谈战略（strategy）。”这可不只是“我要怎么做对标（benchmark）？”那类问题——那其实是我们漏斗顶端（top-of-the-funnel），大家都想知道自己和别人比起来怎么样。
text_es: La gracia fue que, cuando nos reunimos con Gartner, nos dijeron algo así como: "Su superpoder aquí fue que consiguieron que la gente hiciera estrategia sin darse cuenta". Y no era solo "¿cómo me comparo (benchmark)?"; eso fue como nuestra parte alta del embudo (top-of-the-funnel). Todo el mundo quiere saber cómo se compara.
key_sentence: Your superpower here was that you tricked people into strategy.
original_text: And the joke there when we met with Gartner, they were like, "Your superpower here was that you tricked people into strategy," which was not only how do I benchmark? That was kind of our top-of-the-funnel. Everyone wants to know how they compare. But the important thing is what should you do next? What's the most important next step?

vocabulary.definition: A benchmark is a standard or point of reference against which things may be compared or assessed.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, benchmarks are often used to evaluate performance metrics, such as financial results or operational efficiency, allowing companies to gauge their standing relative to competitors.
vocabulary.nuance: While benchmarks provide valuable insights, they can sometimes lead to complacency if organizations focus solely on meeting these standards rather than innovating beyond them.

vocabulary.definition: Top-of-the-funnel refers to the initial stage in the sales and marketing process where potential customers first become aware of a product or service.
vocabulary.businessContext: In marketing, strategies aimed at the top-of-the-funnel focus on attracting leads through awareness campaigns, content marketing, and social media engagement.
vocabulary.nuance: This term emphasizes the importance of generating interest and leads, but it does not address the subsequent stages of the sales process where conversion occurs.

vocabulary.definition: A strategy is a plan of action designed to achieve a long-term or overall aim.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, strategy encompasses the formulation of plans that guide an organization’s direction, resource allocation, and competitive positioning in the market.
vocabulary.nuance: While strategy implies a thoughtful and deliberate approach, it can also carry the connotation of rigidity if not adaptable to changing circumstances.

text: And when I first started ITIL and ITSM, right, the old school kind of change management processes, the common knowledge was that you had to have at least a two-week wait for change approvals in order to get that stability. Turns out that's not right.
speaker: Nicole Forsgren
context: Nicole is explaining how traditional IT service management approaches were based on incorrect assumptions. ITIL (Information Technology Infrastructure Library) and ITSM (IT Service Management) were established frameworks that required lengthy approval processes for any system changes, based on the belief that waiting would improve stability. Her research proved this conventional wisdom was actually counterproductive.
text_ko: 제가 처음 ITIL(ITIL)과 IT 서비스 관리(ITSM)를 시작했을 때요, 옛날식 변경 관리(change management) 프로세스가 주류였어요. 안정성을 위해 변경 승인(change approvals)을 받으려면 적어도 2주는 기다려야 한다는 게 일반적인 상식이었는데, 알고 보니 그게 아니더라고요.
text_zh: 我刚开始接触 ITIL 和 ITSM (ITIL and ITSM) 的时候，按照老一套的变更管理流程 (change management processes)，大家都以为变更审批至少要等两周才能保证稳定性，后来发现并不是这样。
text_es: Y cuando empecé en ITIL e ITSM, ya sabes, con los procesos de gestión de cambios (change management) de la vieja escuela, lo que se daba por hecho era que tenías que esperar al menos dos semanas para las aprobaciones de cambios (change approvals) para conseguir esa estabilidad. Resulta que no es así.
key_sentence: The two-week wait for change approvals was just an old wives' tale.
original_text: And when I first started ITIL and ITSM, right, the old school kind of change management processes, the common knowledge was that you had to have at least a two-week wait for change approvals in order to get that stability. Turns out that's not right. It was just kind of an old wives' tale, right.

vocabulary.definition: Change management refers to the structured approach to transitioning individuals, teams, and organizations from a current state to a desired future state, particularly in the context of organizational change.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology settings, change management is crucial for implementing new processes, systems, or technologies while minimizing disruption and ensuring stakeholder buy-in.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often implies a formalized process that includes planning, communication, and training, and is typically used in contexts where significant changes are anticipated.

vocabulary.definition: Approvals are formal permissions or consents required to proceed with a specific action or decision within an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, approvals are often necessary for project initiation, budget allocation, or changes in policy, ensuring that decisions align with organizational goals and compliance standards.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a bureaucratic process, and its use may vary based on the level of authority required for different types of decisions.

vocabulary.definition: Stability refers to the state of being steady, consistent, and resistant to change, particularly in organizational performance or systems.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, stability is essential for maintaining operational efficiency, customer trust, and overall organizational health, especially during periods of change.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often connotes a sense of reliability and predictability, and is typically used in discussions about risk management and organizational resilience.

text: We want to implement good technical practices like automated testing, good architectural practices so that when you move fast, you are also more stable, right.
speaker: Nicole Forsgren
context: Nicole is explaining the core principle behind effective DevOps practices. Rather than simply removing all safety measures to move faster, the goal is to implement proper technical foundations like automated testing and good system architecture. This allows teams to achieve both speed and stability simultaneously, while also improving the overall developer experience through better tooling and processes.
text_ko: 우리는 자동화 테스트(automated testing)나 탄탄한 아키텍처 관행(architectural practices) 같은 좋은 기술 관행을 적용해서, 속도를 내도 안정적으로 운영될 수 있게 하고 싶어요.
text_zh: 我们想把一些好的技术做法落地，比如自动化测试 (automated testing) 和良好的架构实践 (architectural practices)，这样在快速推进的时候也能更稳些，对吧？
text_es: Queremos adoptar buenas prácticas técnicas, como pruebas automatizadas (automated testing) y buenas prácticas de arquitectura (architectural practices), para que al movernos rápido también seamos más estables.
key_sentence: we want to implement good technical practices like automated testing, good architectural practices so that when you move fast, you are also more stable
original_text: We want to implement good technical practices like automated testing, good architectural practices so that when you move fast, you are also more stable, right. We want to be thinking about improving the developer experience so that when we are faster, we are also saving time.

vocabulary.definition: To put a plan or decision into effect; to execute a strategy or process.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, implementing often refers to the execution of new systems, processes, or policies to improve efficiency or achieve specific goals.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'implement' suggests a proactive approach to execution, it can imply a degree of complexity or difficulty in the transition from planning to action.

vocabulary.definition: A software testing technique that uses automated tools to execute test cases and compare actual outcomes with expected results.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech startups, automated testing is crucial for ensuring software quality and accelerating the development process by allowing for rapid feedback on code changes.
vocabulary.nuance: While automated testing increases efficiency, it may not catch all issues, so it is often used in conjunction with manual testing for comprehensive coverage.

vocabulary.definition: The methodologies and principles guiding the design and structure of software systems and applications.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, good architectural practices ensure that software is scalable, maintainable, and aligned with business objectives, facilitating long-term success.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a connotation of strategic foresight and planning, emphasizing the importance of foundational design in achieving operational efficiency.

vocabulary.definition: Characterized by consistency and reliability; not prone to sudden changes or failures.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology and business, stability is critical for systems and processes to ensure user trust and operational continuity, especially during rapid growth phases.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'stable' conveys a positive quality, it can also imply a lack of innovation or adaptability if overemphasized in a fast-paced environment.

text: Most people only think about this from the speed standpoint, which means when you move faster, you are more stable, which means you're pushing smaller changes more often, right.
speaker: Nicole Forsgren
context: Nicole is explaining one of her key research findings about the relationship between deployment frequency and system stability. She's describing how the DORA metrics revealed that speed and stability move together - teams that deploy more frequently actually have more stable systems. This counterintuitive finding occurs because frequent deployments involve smaller changes that are easier to debug when problems arise.
text_ko: 대부분 사람들은 이걸 속도 관점(speed standpoint)에서만 생각해요. 즉 빨리 움직일수록 더 안정적이고, 그건 작은 변경을 더 자주 적용한다는 뜻이에요, 그렇죠?
text_zh: 大多数人只从速度这个角度看这事，觉得你动作越快就越稳，也就是说会更频繁地推出更小的改动，对吧？
text_es: La mayoría de la gente solo lo ve en términos de velocidad: creen que si te mueves más rápido eres más estable, es decir, que vas introduciendo cambios más pequeños con más frecuencia, ¿no?
key_sentence: when you move faster, you are more stable, which means you're pushing smaller changes more often
original_text: Most people only think about this from the speed standpoint, which means when you move faster, you are more stable, which means you're pushing smaller changes more often, right. Because if you're pushing all the time, it's going to be very, very small changes, which means you have a smaller blast radius, which means when you push, you have an error in production. It's going to be easier to debug, right.
